title: Samsung says a third-party provider for its North American ad business had a cybersecurity incident; n0n gang claimed a leak
date_note: Date of the n0n leak claim as published by Technext (19 November); Sina (24 November) reports Samsung's later statement. The articles give no date for the leak itself.
place: South Korea (company's home country as the article states)
geo_basis: country as stated ('South Korean tech giant'); no city given
summary: Sina, relaying overseas media, reports Samsung Electronics said a cybersecurity incident hit a third-party provider that processes data for its North American advertising business, and that a preliminary review found some Samsung data may be affected. Samsung is investigating with the provider and has not said how many users are affected, per Sina. Technext, citing Cybernews, earlier reported a gang called n0n allegedly dumped 220MB of data.
plain: Samsung reportedly says a provider handling data for its North American ad business had a security incident, and some Samsung data may be affected. It has not said how many users. A gang had claimed a 220MB leak.
exec: Samsung reportedly acknowledges a third-party provider incident that may affect some of its data; user numbers are not disclosed.
action: No action needed; for awareness. Samsung says it will disclose more as the investigation progresses, per Sina.
impact: Samsung has not disclosed the number of affected users, per Sina.

evidence.quote: A ransomware gang called n0n has allegedly dumped 220MB of the data on the dark web.

sources.name: Sina Finance, 24 November 2026 (relaying overseas media; Samsung statement)

validation.note: Samsung statement known only through Sina, relaying unnamed overseas media; Samsung's own page not found. Technext relays Cybernews on the claim.

report.note: Sina and Technext articles read; Samsung original and Cybernews original not read.
